title: Lipase inhibitory activity assay for fermented milk
author: Gil-Rodríguez, Beresford
materials: •Reagents○Trizma base○Trizma-HCl○Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO)○Lipase from porcine pancreas, Type II○4-nitrophenyl octanoate (NPC)○Clarifying reagent for dairy products (Sigma Aldrich, cat no. 00,467–500ML)○Orlistat (to use as positive control)•Consumables○5 mL tubes○2.5 – 3 mL syringes○0.2 µm PES filters○Plastic cuvettes for spectrophotometry○Capillary pistons for positive displacement pipette•Equipment○Spectrophotometer○Vortex with adapter for at least 20 tubes○Water bath○Positive displacement pipette○Timer

steps.title: Prepare Tris–HCl buffers
steps.instruction: Make two 0.10 M Tris–HCl solutions: one with Trizma‑base, one with Trizma‑HCl. Mix them to obtain pH 8.8 (for the pH 8.5 assay buffer) and pH 9.8 (for the pH 9.5 assay buffer) at room temperature (19–21 °C). Verify the pH after heating an aliquot to 37 °C (target 8.5 and 9.5). Prepare the buffers at least one day before the assay, store at room temperature overnight, re‑check and adjust pH if needed, then filter‑sterilize into sterile bottles.

steps.title: Prepare lipase stock solution
steps.instruction: Label twenty 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes. In a small glass beaker add 2 mL Tris–HCl buffer pH 8.5, place a magnetic stir bar, and set the beaker on ice in a stir plate running at low speed. Weigh 100 mg porcine pancreatic lipase (Type II) and add it slowly to the buffer in small portions, stirring continuously for 5 min to dissolve completely without bubbles. While still on ice, dispense the solution into 100 µL aliquots in the labeled tubes and freeze immediately at –20 °C. This creates a 50 mg mL⁻¹ lipase stock.

steps.title: Prepare lipase working solution
steps.instruction: Just before the assay, add 900 µL Tris–HCl buffer pH 8.5 (37 °C) to one frozen 100 µL lipase stock aliquot. Mix gently by pipetting, then invert the tube several times (do not vortex). The resulting solution is 5 mg mL⁻¹ lipase; discard any unused material after the assay.

steps.title: Prepare NPC stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 4‑nitrophenyl octanoate (NPC) in DMSO to a concentration of 50 mM (10× the working concentration). For 5 mL of 50 mM stock, weigh 66.325 mg NPC; using its density (1.095 g mL⁻¹) this corresponds to 60.57 µL DMSO. Aliquot 100 µL portions into brown 1.5 mL tubes and store at 4 °C (do not freeze). Before the assay, let the tubes thaw at room temperature for at least 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare NPC working solution
steps.instruction: Add 900 µL DMSO to one 100 µL NPC stock aliquot to obtain a 5 mM NPC working solution.

steps.title: Prepare orlistat control solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5.2 mg orlistat in 1 mL DMSO to obtain a 10 mg mL⁻¹ solution (used as the positive‑inhibition control).

steps.title: Label reaction tubes
steps.instruction: Label 5 mL tubes in duplicate for each condition (maximum 20 tubes per run): B (blank), C (100 % activity control), O (orlistat control, when used), BM (blank for non‑fermented milk control), M (non‑fermented milk control), and three sample tubes with their respective blanks.

steps.title: Add Tris–HCl buffer
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of Tris–HCl buffer to each tube according to Table 1: B 2.55 mL, C 2.50 mL, O 2.45 mL, BM 2 mL, M 2 mL, each sample 2 mL. This brings the total volume to 2.60 mL after all reagents are added.

steps.title: Add milk samples and controls
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of non‑fermented milk to tube M and to each sample tube. Add 500 µL of fermented milk to the sample tubes (as indicated). No milk is added to B, C, O, or BM.

steps.title: Add NPC or DMSO
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the 5 mM NPC working solution to tubes C, O, BM, M, and each sample. For blank tubes B, add 50 µL DMSO instead of NPC.

steps.title: Add lipase solution
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the 5 mg mL⁻¹ lipase working solution to every tube (B, C, O, BM, M, and all samples).

steps.title: Vortex reaction mixture
steps.instruction: Place all tubes in a vortex adapter and vortex for 2 min (all tubes simultaneously).

steps.title: Incubate enzymatic reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes in a water bath set to 37 °C for 30 min. Start a timer when the incubation begins.

steps.title: Add clarifying reagent
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of the clarifying reagent for dairy products to each tube. Mix gently by inversion (do not vortex) to avoid foaming.

steps.title: Clarify and incubate
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes for 3 min at 37 °C in the water bath.

steps.title: Transfer and filter if needed
steps.instruction: Transfer 2.7 mL of each clarified mixture into a plastic cuvette. If turbidity remains, filter the transferred liquid through a 0.2 µm PES filter before measurement.

steps.title: Measure absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance of each cuvette at 412 nm using a spectrophotometer. Use a positive‑displacement pipette for handling coagulated milk samples and clarifying reagent.

steps.title: Calculate inhibition
steps.instruction: Correct each sample absorbance by subtracting a 5.71 % (average 5.74 %) reduction caused by milk solids. Then compute lipase inhibitory activity (%) with: 100 − [(AbsS − AbsSB) / (AbsRC − AbsB) × 100], where AbsS is the corrected sample absorbance, AbsSB the corresponding blank, AbsRC the 100 % activity control absorbance, and AbsB its blank.
